audit_point: pre-upgrade baseline (branch chore/metaobjects-1.0, cut from origin/main at f14546d)

versions.latest_available_note: npm latest is 0.25.x; this project is 10 minor lines behind.

scorecard.next_unmet_check: Exemplary needs (a) no dead generated/scaffolded artifacts and (b) the committed .gen-state/.hashes.json ownership record — see findings dead-scaffolded-generators and gen-state-hashes-gitignored.

pillars.top_gap: two scaffolded owned generators (queries.ts, routes.ts, 202 LOC) are wired to nothing and are never compiled against the package's evolving API by any gate that matters
no database, no ObjectManager, no routes — the runtime surface is the render Provider + generated value-object types, and both are wired correctly
verify --codegen is not run; CI uses the sanctioned equivalent (meta gen + git diff --exit-code), so coverage is complete
none — every prompt and email body is a declared template with an external @textRef/@subjectRef/@htmlBodyRef/@textBodyRef and a typed object.value payload

scorecard.ci_drift_gate_detail: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `bun run gen` then `git diff --exit-code` then `bun run verify` (= `meta verify --prompts templates`) then `bun test` then `bun run build`. test/drift.test.ts additionally PROVES the gates bite, by mutating a temp copy of the repo in four ways and asserting a non-zero meta exit each time.

census.leverage_ratio_note: 396 generated / (225 metadata + 811 authored generator+provider). LOW, and legitimately so: this project's return on MetaObjects is not code volume, it is (a) a closed, loader-enforced vocabulary for its own domain concepts and (b) four drift gates that fail the build. Do not read this number as under-adoption.

coverage_matrix.gated_by: meta gen (baked verify: field list -> ERR_VAR_NOT_ON_PAYLOAD); NOT by verify --templates

findings.title: the codegen ownership record (.gen-state/.hashes.json) is gitignored, so no fresh clone or CI runner can tell 'we wrote this' from 'somebody edited this'
findings.evidence: .metaobjects/.gitignore line 1 is `.gen-state/` — the whole directory. `git ls-files | grep gen-state` returns nothing, while `.metaobjects/.gen-state/.hashes.json` exists on disk. Doctrine: the snapshot BODIES are gitignored, `.hashes.json` is COMMITTED.
findings.impact: On a fresh clone (which is every CI run) meta gen has neither a snapshot body nor a recorded hash, so an out-of-date committed generated file is REFUSED by name rather than merged or overwritten. Today CI is green only because every generated file happens to be byte-current.
findings.next_command: un-ignore .gen-state/.hashes.json in .metaobjects/.gitignore and commit the file
findings.parity_gate: git ls-files .metaobjects/.gen-state/.hashes.json is non-empty; `bun run gen` from a fresh clone still reports 14 unchanged

findings.title: two scaffolded owned generators (queries.ts, routes.ts) are imported by nothing and gated by nothing
findings.evidence: `git grep 'generators/queries\|generators/routes'` matches only the two files' own headers and the vendored skill docs — metaobjects.config.ts imports neither. The config comment says so explicitly: 'the routes/queries generators + apiPrefix that WOULD consume them are removed.'
findings.impact: 202 LOC of package-vintage template code that will silently rot against the package API. They compile today only because tsconfig has no `include` and so sweeps them up; nothing else asserts anything about them.
findings.next_command: delete codegen/generators/queries.ts and codegen/generators/routes.ts (re-obtainable at any time with `meta eject queries` / `meta eject routes`)
findings.parity_gate: tsc --noEmit exit 0 and `bun run gen` still reports the same 14 files

findings.title: metaobjects.config.ts declares dbImport + dialect purely to satisfy a type, on a project with no database
findings.evidence: The config's own comment: 'dbImport/dialect are required by MetaobjectsGenConfig even though smon declares only value objects (no write-through entities), so no DB code is generated and these go unused. Kept to satisfy the type'.
findings.impact: Two lies in the config file. A reader is told the project has a sqlite database and a ../db module; neither exists.
findings.next_command: drop both keys once the package stops demanding them
findings.parity_gate: `bun run gen` emits the same 14 files

findings.title: the render-helper generator emits a .js import extension while the project declares extStyle: "none"
findings.evidence: AlertEmail.render.ts line 3 is `import type { AlertPayload } from "./AlertPayload.js";` while src/generated/index.ts (barrel) emits `export * from "./AlertPayload";` — same run, same config, two answers.
findings.impact: Cosmetic here (moduleResolution: bundler tolerates both) but it is one config knob answered two ways by two generators in one run — the exact defect class 0.25.0 spent its breaking slot on. PRODUCT-SIDE, not adopter fault.

findings.title: the two *.render.ts files carry no @generated marker
findings.evidence: Both files start directly with `import { render } from "@metaobjectsdev/render";`. Every other generated file in src/generated/ starts with `// @generated by @metaobjectsdev/codegen-ts — DO NOT EDIT.`
findings.impact: A human opening the file has no signal it is generated. The overwrite decision does not read the header, so nothing breaks — it is a documentation inconsistency. PRODUCT-SIDE.

findings.title: metaobjects/meta.common.json declares nothing, under a bare `metadata` key and an empty package
findings.evidence: Whole file: {"metadata": {"package": "", "children": []}} — a bare `metadata` type key (not `metadata.root`) with zero children, while the two real files use `metadata.root` and package `smon`.
findings.impact: Zero today. It is also this project's canary for 0.25.0's bare-type-key parser fix (four parsers previously answered a bare key three different wrong ways); if it survives the upgrade the fix reaches this shape correctly.
findings.next_command: delete the file, or give it the abstract BaseEntity content its name promises

findings.title: adapter.notify's @kind enum mixes transport with role
findings.evidence: ADAPTER_KINDS = push | heartbeat | chat | email | stdout. Four of those are transports; `heartbeat` is a ROLE (kuma is an HTTP push whose semantics are 'liveness', and src/cli.ts + src/notify/registry.ts both special-case `name === "kuma"` in code rather than dispatching on a declared fact).
findings.impact: ADVISORY. The `kuma is not an alert channel` rule is hand-coded in two places (src/cli.ts defaultNotifyPort, src/notify/registry.ts's one-type-param satisfies pin) when it could be a declared property of the node. Low blast radius: one adapter.
findings.metadata_sketch: adapter.notify Kuma: @kind: "push" plus a new boolean @alertChannel: false (ADR-0037 step 2b — it modifies an existing type, it does not own behavior of its own), letting notify-registry.ts emit the exclusion instead of cli.ts hard-coding the name.
findings.parity_gate: test/cli.test.ts's kuma-is-not-an-alert-channel cases still pass with the name literal removed from src/cli.ts

findings.title: no requirement.* nodes; this project's rules live in prose
findings.evidence: The CI workflow header is 15 lines of prose explaining which of four gates catches which class of drift; src/cli.ts carries a 19-line PARITY NOTES block asserting behavioural equivalences with a bash reference. None of it is checkable.
findings.impact: ADVISORY and OPT-IN — an absent ledger is not a defect. Recorded so the AFTER audit can say whether the upgrade changed anything here; authoring a first ledger is out of scope for an upgrade.
findings.next_command: none — deliberately not authored during the 1.0 pass

non_findings_verified: own*() accessor discipline (ADR-0039): CLEAN. The only isArray hits in codegen/ and src/ are JavaScript's Array.isArray(); no ownAttr/ownChildren/ownFields anywhere. All three custom generators read node.attr(name), the resolving accessor.
hand-rolled prompt strings: NONE. Every prompt and email body is an external .mustache resolved through @textRef/@subjectRef/@htmlBodyRef/@textBodyRef.

hand-rolled output parsing: NOT APPLICABLE. enrich() JSON.parses the `claude -p --output-format json` TRANSPORT envelope and reads .result; the model's own answer is free-form prose, so there is no response shape to declare and no @responseRef is owed.
hand-written SQL / views / migrations: NONE. This project has no database at all — every object is an object.value, state is per-probe JSON on disk.

hand-written validators shadowing a generated schema: NONE. src/config.ts validates SMON_NOTIFY/SMON_PROBES against the GENERATED closed sets (AdapterName from registry.data.ts, ProbeName from roster.ts) rather than re-listing them.

N declarations of one shape: NONE. src/notify/registry.ts spreads ...ADAPTERS[name] rather than restating the entry, and pins each impl with `satisfies NotifyAdapter<...>` against the generated payload types.
template-text duplication: NONE. Seven .mustache files, no two structurally identical (alert vs digest are genuinely different documents).

custom vocabulary vs ADR-0037: adapter.notify and probe.bash both pass the ordered test — each is a domain concept owning its own attributes and its own loader-enforced validation (ERR_SMON_TAG_GRAMMAR, ERR_SMON_EMAIL_TEMPLATE_REQUIRED, ERR_SMON_TEMPLATE_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH), not a modifier on an existing type. This is the axis-I 'new-vocabulary OPPORTUNITY' hunt already executed by the adopter.
